subject: SUM function
notes:
Citation re-derived mechanically: `cite.py --check 15.88.3 "Argument-1 shall be of class numeric"` => OK, §15.88.3 rule 1 (Argument rule). READ: IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs#Verified row `["SUM"] = Uniform('n', "§15.88.3 r1")` (line 693, in the 'statistical trio' block beside STANDARD-DEVIATION and VARIANCE); IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs#Uniform builds an ArgSchema with EMPTY positional kinds and a TAIL rule, so `schema.At(i)` yields the 'n' rule for EVERY argument position — which is what §15.88.2's repeated `{ argument-1 }` needs, since every written argument IS argument-1. Enforcement: IntrinsicBinder.cs#CheckArgumentClasses (line 1652) is called on the generic path at line 587, AFTER arity and BEFORE every per-function arm; it loops all positions and calls IntrinsicArgumentRules.Violation. For kind 'n', Violation reads CandidateClasses(op) and Admissible('n') = [CobolClass.Numeric] — so a numeric-EDITED item (Table 2 class alphanumeric, mapped to CobolClass.NumericEditedDeEditing) is rejected too, which the arm's comment derives from §8.8.1.1 ("an identifier referencing a NUMERIC DATA ITEM"). VERIFIED EDGES: (a) a GROUP argument — ClassOfPlace returns Alphanumeric for `Item.IsGroup` (National/Boolean for an as-if-pic group), so `FUNCTION SUM(grp)` is rejected; (b) an INDEX item — the usage-keyed arm returns CobolClass.Index before the category table, so it cannot pass as numeric; (c) a table(ALL) argument — TableAllPlace is a `PlaceDecorator(Element)` (Place.cs:158), so `p.Item` is the ELEMENT and the element's class is screened, i.e. `SUM(alphaTable(ALL))` is rejected, not failed open; (d) the figurative ZERO is admissible here by §8.3.3.6.4 GR4 (CandidateClasses gives it Numeric among four), correct behavior per the batch's rule 8. FAIL-OPEN residue, deliberate and documented at the Violation head: an operand whose class is not statically decidable (candidates empty) is not screened — that can only miss a rejection, never invent one. TESTS: tests/conformance/negative/pb58-sum-alpha.cob (`COMPUTE R = FUNCTION SUM(N9 X3)`, header cites "ISO 15.88.3 r1", reject-at 2002 2014 2023, expected diagnostic COBOL1627 in the .err, registered in tests/conformance/negative/manifest.json:192) and the positive twin tests/conformance/2023/pb58_argument_predicates_legal.cob line 75 (`FUNCTION SUM(N9 I2 3.5)` — registered in tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json:124). Nothing missing for this rule.

REFUTER (verdict SUSTAINED after independent attack): citation re-derived independently — `cite.py --check 15.88.3 "Argument-1 shall be of class numeric"` => OK, §15.88.3 rule 1; spec text re-read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:33501-33504. Attacked on four axes and each held. (1) TWO-ARM DISPATCH (the shape that has recurred five times in this repo): both `functionCall` alternatives that can spell SUM — the FUNCTION-keyword arm (IntrinsicBinder.cs:89) and the reserved-word keyword-omitted arm `SUM(…)` (IntrinsicBinder.cs:78, CobolExpressions.g4#reservedIntrinsicArgFn) — converge on the SAME BindIntrinsicCore (line 438), whose generic path calls CheckArgumentClasses; there is no unscreened second route, and KeywordOmittedFunction cannot reach SUM at all because a reserved word never arrives in the cobolWord name slot. (2) ArgSchema.At(i) (IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs:172) returns the Tail rule for EVERY i when Positions is empty, so Uniform('n') genuinely screens all n positions of the repeated argument-1, not just position 1. (3) The two classifier holes I probed are closed: a ref-modified numeric item resolves through RefModPlace.Category (Place.cs:292ff), which implements §8.4.3.3.4 GR6 c) — numeric under display usage is considered class alphanumeric — so `FUNCTION SUM(N9(1:2))` is rejected; and a nested USER-DEFINED function result does NOT fall into the fail-open `BoundComputedOperand => CobolClass.Numeric` catch-all, because UdfBinder.UdfBindCall returns `new BoundNumRef(tempPlace)` over a temp cloned from the RETURNING item's description (§8.4.3.2.4 GR1), so it reaches the screen as a BoundFieldOperand carrying the real category and an alphanumeric-returning UDF is rejected. (4) EDITIONS: CheckArgumentClasses is gated only on `ctx.Edition.Permissive`, never on the edition, so the screen fires at --std 85 as well; the negative fixture's `reject-at: 2002 2014 2023` omits 85 only because that same fixture declares `01 TDEF TYPEDEF STRONG` and `01 NAT PIC N(2)`, both COBOL-2002+ constructs that would make an 85 run reject for the wrong reason — not because the rule is edition-gated. Verdict held at CONFORMS.
